newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends weak, Brent slide gathers pace.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends weak, Brent slide gathers pace.

text.p: IPE gas oil ended weak on Tuesday, outstripping losses on Brent crude which slid through support levels against a weak fundamental background, brokers said.
June gas oil shed $4 to close at $170 a tonne. By 1700 GMT, July Brent was trading at $19 a barrel, down 52 cents on Monday's close.
"The market this morning didn't have a view and was pretty passive but this afternoon we've started to get some price action without any particular news," said a senior broker.
July Brent pierced support around $19.10 a barrel as traders and investment funds joined an early local-led selling spree.
"There was trade selling of the spreads and outright price and as the market hit new lows it attracted heavier fund activity," said a broker.
Dealers said technical support at $19 on July Brent appeared to be holding but a break below the psychological level would open the way for further losses down to $18.88 last seen three weeks ago.
Expectations that American Petroleum Institute (API) figures due to be released later on Tuesday would show U.S. crude stocks rising further due to a flood of imports dented sentiment, they said.
Brokers would also be watching the API data for further evidence of the strength of U.S. gasoline demand which typically sets the pace for oil markets during the early summer.
"We're expecting a slight build given the high refinery throughputs," said a broker.
Also keeping dealers on their toes were continuing discussions in New York aimed at agreeing an extension of the six-month U.N. oil-for-food deal which expires on Saturday.
U.N. Security Council members are scheduled to meet on Tuesday to draft a resolution to allow the pact's renewal, probably by Friday at the latest. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7930
